items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The manager was Harold Johnson and a great barman called Lew... Lew who served us... Lew was very heavy-handed with us when we went into the bar for a drink... Lew didn't serve the clientele in this manner but he liked performers and that's why he was a great barman to me.

ctx.x: The drummer was a fellow named Yank Porter who had worked a long time at the Harlem club and I had known him for years. Benny Morton was the trombonist, Jimmie Hamilton, a clarinetist whom I didn't know before, and Al Hall, whom I had seen in Teddy's big band, was the bass player.

This club, which was actually called Cafe Society Downtown, was at Sheridan Square and was owned by a man named Barney Josephson. The manager was Harold Johnson and a great barman called Lew. I will mention why Lew was a great barman to me later. There were four acts in the show and I know that three of them were discovered by and sponsored by John Hammond.

Boogie Woogie was popular and John had put it together the three greatest exponents of that style of piano playing. They were Meade Lux Lewis, Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons. But the Cafe only Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons were working as a team, and there was a great blues singer named "Big" Joe Turner whom the two boogie woogie pianists accompanied. And the three of them would really rock the joint every night. And they could drink plenty of booze and carry it well.
